name: publicWeb_getPageLayout
description: Returns the saved Puck page layout JSON blob for a kennel. Uses LEFT JOIN so kennels without a KennelWebsite row return one row with PageLayoutJson = NULL rather than zero rows (which the shim would misread as 404). Callers fall back to the hardcoded default layout when the value is NULL. No authentication required.

parameters.name: KennelSlug
parameters.description: URL slug of the kennel whose layout to load. No SQL default.

rowsets.name: PageLayoutResult
rowsets.description: Always one row for a valid active kennel. Zero rows means kennel not found or inactive — shim returns 404. One row with PageLayoutJson NULL means the kennel exists but has no saved layout yet.

columns.name: PageLayoutJson
columns.description: JSON blob of shape PageLayoutBlob = Partial<Record<PageType, Data>> where PageType is 'home'|'runs'|'about'|'events'|'songs'|'stats'. NULL when no layout has been saved.

rowsets.name: CatchEnvelope
rowsets.description: Only on a runtime error: { Success = 0, ErrorMessage } instead of the layout row. The error is neither logged nor re-raised.

codeSmells.issue: CATCH does not log to HC.ErrorLog
codeSmells.detail: Lines 32-34 turn any runtime error into a { Success = 0, ErrorMessage } row with no HC.ErrorLog record and no THROW. The Next.js caller reads rowset 0 for PageLayoutJson, finds no such column, and falls back to the default layout — so a failure is silent: the kennel's saved layout just disappears from the page.

@KennelSlug have no SQL default (line 2). A caller that omits one is refused by SQL Server before the procedure runs — an empty 500 with no HC.ErrorLog row (CLAUDE.md 'SP parameter with NO default'). The Next.js client always sends them, so this is latent.

Returns the layout even when the kennel website is disabled (Enabled = 0). This is intentional — the admin editor needs to load the layout regardless of published state — but callers rendering the public page should independently check WebsiteEnabled before rendering.

breakingChangeRules: Never change the zero-row = 404 / null-value = no layout contract — Next.js callers depend on this distinction
Never change from LEFT JOIN to INNER JOIN — that would break the null-layout signal
